newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha steady to firmer on tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha steady to firmer on tight supplies.

text.p: Naphtha prices were steady to a touch firmer in Friday afternoon Tokyo trade due to tight supplies for prompt cargoes as well as crude gains on the ACCESS after-hours trading system, traders said.
Open-specification naphtha for first-half March was assessed at $239.00/240.50, up from late Thursday's $238.50/239.50.
Second-half February was quoted at $243.00/244.50, compared with $242.00/243.00 on Thursday.
In naphtha's inter-month spreads, first-half March/first-half April was discussed at plus $5.50/6.50.
Second-half March/second-half April and first-half April/first-half May were both indicated at plus $5.00/6.00.

In middle distillates trading, spot jet cargoes were notionally assessed at $2.20 to $2.30 over the mean of Singapore quote on a cost and freight (C and F) basis. Dual purpose kerosene cargoes were assessed 20 to 30 cents higher than the jet cargo levels, traders said.
Japan Energy brought its 110,000 barrel-per-day topper at its Mizushima refinery back on line on Friday afternoon. It had been closed since December 18 due to a gas leak.
